rules.rule: A bright patch is a highlight (specular) if it moves when the viewer moves, whereas diffuse shading remains fixed relative to the object's geometry.
rules.evidence: So the specular highlight moves when you move; the diffuse shading does not. That one test tells you whether a bright patch is a highlight or a light-coloured piece of paint, and it costs nothing but a head movement.

rules.rule: If a highlight matches the object's body colour, the material is likely metal, which reflects almost no of its own colour.
rules.evidence: Anything with a highlight the same colour as its own body is either metal or wrong — go to Metal and everything else.

rules.rule: A perfectly diffuse surface is physically unrealisable; real matte surfaces rely on internal scattering rather than outer roughness.
rules.evidence: PBRT points out a perfectly diffuse surface is not physically realisable; dull chalkboard and matte paint are the closest real things
